title: fix(test): remaining suites time out on their first test or hook while compiled worker subprocesses prepare
body:
Related: #162792 (follow-up; it left these suites for an SDK decision and core splits), #161637

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the first test or hook of 70 more Vitest files (extension, package, and oversized core suites) absorbs the one-time compiled worker preparation (tens of seconds warm, minutes cold) and slows down or times out, because the file first reaches a compiled-subprocess declaration inside a test body or hook instead of at collection.

## User Impact

No product change. Developers running `pnpm test <file>` and CI shards whose first declaration load came from one of these files no longer pay the worker preparation inside a test or hook deadline; it happens during collection, where #156011 and #162792 put it.

## Why This Change Was Made

#162792 fixed 335 files but could not reach the rest: extensions and packages cannot import core test utilities, and three core files were already over the line cap. This PR closes those gaps at the owner of each lazy load:

- **New repo-local SDK preload.** `openclaw/plugin-sdk/compiled-subprocess-testing` is one side-effect line, `import "../test-utils/prepare-compiled-subprocesses.js";`, with no exports. It is registered like `test-node-mocks` and `sqlite-runtime-testing`: private-local-only, non-production, excluded from npm `files` and package exports, absent from the production build. The public SDK entrypoint set and export map are unchanged. Agreed with the SDK owner before adding it.
- **Shared Codex owner.** 35 Codex app-server deadline rows came from one place: the `test/setup.extensions.ts` `beforeEach` that calls `vi.importActual("../src/infra/worker-cpu.js")` for every `extensions/codex/src/app-server/*.test.ts` file. Setup now imports only the declaration preload for that path pattern at setup evaluation. The `worker-cpu` import itself stays in the `beforeEach`, after each file's mocks are registered, so no module binds earlier than before. One shared constant drives both checks. Every one of the 319 matching files already loaded a declaration through that hook whenever a case ran. The 15 that can skip every case on some platform already reach one statically, so no consumer starts loading one.
- **Per-file preloads (29 suites).** These suites re-import their subject per test (`vi.resetModules`, `vi.doMock`, cold-import guards), or their first load happens inside production code they call: lazy runtimes in Codex, Deepgram, Inworld, Telegram, Ollama, OpenAI OAuth, the memory-host auth adapter, and others. Extensions and the package use the SDK subpath. Core suites use the core module directly.
- **Static imports (3 suites).** `anthropic/cli-auth-seam`, plus the DeepInfra and xAI video transport suites. Their one-time subject import moved from a test or `beforeAll` to collection, with the same reset, unmock, and mock order (`vi.hoisted(() => vi.resetModules())`, an existing idiom).
- **Owner splits of the three line-capped core files.** `run-main.exit` splits into exit, gateway startup, command dispatch, and bare-root onboarding. `media/fetch` splits into reads and store. The official external catalog splits into metadata and hosted feed. Test names, assertions, and counts are unchanged (111 = 11+26+46+28, 72 = 28+44, 38 = 14+24). Only the six parts that load a declaration take the preload. The trimmed `run-main.exit` and catalog-metadata files stay declaration-free. Their max-lines baseline entries are removed, along with one already-stale entry the ratchet flagged (`chat.abort-persistence.test.ts`).
- **Protected CI selection follows the split.** The four destination suites that received protected `run-main.exit` and catalog cases join `PR_PROTECTED_RUNTIME_TEST_FILES`, so global inputs such as `pnpm-lock.yaml` still select them. The existing global-input planner test asserts this (ClawSweeper finding).
- **Bounded cleanups the gates required.** `sanitizeJitiCachePathSegment` moved unchanged into `sdk-alias-normalization.ts` so the baselined `sdk-alias.ts` does not grow. Five unused exports were dropped from the new CLI test-support module (dead-export scan).
- **Docs.** `docs/help/testing/writing-tests.md`, `docs/plugins/sdk-subpaths.md`, and `docs/plugins/sdk-testing.md` document the extension preload and when to use it.

No timeouts, retries, configs, worker pins, or assertions changed.

## Evidence

**Finding the files.** A temporary bridge instrumentation (reverted, never committed) recorded each test file's first declaration load against its collection end, using `--isolate` and the repository runner. Controls passed: `host-capability.environment` = collection; `deepgram/audio` = deadline.

The inventory was all 4,683 extension and package test files at base, plus core tests changed on main since #162792's screen base that contain lazy, reset, or mock signals, plus the three named core files: 5,164 files in total.

- **Screened:** every file with a direct lazy-import, reset, or mock signal, and every file in `extensions/a2a` through `extensions/crabbox`. That is 2,194 conclusive files and 45 errored, mostly `*.live.test.ts` paths the ordinary lane excludes.
- **Not screened:** 2,925 lower-priority files that reach a production lazy import only indirectly, or not within three static edges. Testbox jobs are now capped at 60 minutes (#162678), capacity stalled, and local throughput on this shared host was too low. These are left for a follow-up with the same method.

The screens found **70 deadline files**, and all are fixed here. That covers #162792's remaining 52, plus 18 the earlier screen had not reached.

**After-screen.** The instrumentation was re-applied to the final tree for every changed test file, all 35 shared-fix Codex files, 10 Codex controls, and 5 non-Codex controls. Every fixed file loads at collection, the controls are unchanged, and the two declaration-free split files stay `none`.

**Paired timings.** Each pair ran back to back on the same host, base `931c7b40b2e4` vs this branch, with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose --isolate`. "Affected" is the first test or hook that previously loaded the declaration. These are load observations on a shared 32-core host, not a controlled benchmark.

| File | Load | Affected ms, before → after | Vitest Duration, before → after |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `packages/memory-host-sdk/.../embeddings-remote-client` | 33–42 | 65,126 → 4,866 | 68.3 s → 18.1 s |
| `codex/src/node-exec-server` | 35–42 | 62,431 → 7,100 | 74.6 s → 69.4 s |
| `migrate-hermes/model.apply` | 43–49 | 49,752 → 18,028 | 52.4 s → 34.3 s |
| `memory-lancedb/startup-imports` | 34–42 | 36,071 → 12,088 | 38.3 s → 28.6 s |
| `openai/realtime-voice.optional-capture` | 34–43 | 26,838 → 6,248 | 31.4 s → 21.9 s |
| `codex/src/app-server/launch-args` (shared setup) | 33–35 | 26,659 → 186 | 29.7 s → 17.9 s |
| `deepgram/audio` | 35–49 | 22,586 → 4,762 | 28.6 s → 25.3 s |
| `inworld/tts` | 46–49 | 21,172 → 1,747 | 24.8 s → 16.5 s |
| `telegram/audit.transport-close` | 34–36 | 18,073 → 2,791 | 22.8 s → 17.2 s |
| `anthropic/cli-auth-seam` | 62–86 | 120,196 (timeout) → 750 | 318.3 s → 133.6 s |
| `deepinfra` / `xai` video transport (`beforeAll`) | 33–107 | ≥180,000 (timeout) → hook removed | 202.1 → 73.2 s / 186.8 → 142.5 s |
| CLI: newer schema blocks environment selection | 33–107 | 120,059 (timeout) → 8,894 | split file |
| `media/fetch` `beforeAll` | 33–107 | ≥180,000 (timeout) → 4,583 | split file |
| Catalog: schema-v2 state/trust installs | 33–107 | 44,476 → 14,324 | split file |
| `llm-task/index` | 49–67 | 59,708 → 90,891 | 63.7 s → 126.1 s |

The preparation moves; it does not disappear. Affected tests that still take seconds afterwards are transforming a large lazily imported graph inside the test. One pair runs the other way. `llm-task`'s lazy-registration test was slower after the fix at higher, fluctuating load, while the phase screen shows its preparation now at collection. Its remaining cost is the deliberately lazy tool import, and this PR does not change that.

**Correctness.** Every changed test file passed on the final tree: 474 cases across 33 files plus 170 across eight, with three Linux-only skips on macOS. So did all 35 shared-fix Codex files and five unrelated extension controls. The split files keep identical test-name multisets.

**Checks.** `pnpm build` passed. `pnpm tsgo:all` passed. Full lint passed after the build. The Plugin SDK export and surface-budget checks passed (369 total, 154 public, 215 local-only, public set unchanged). The line-cap and max-lines ratchets, the dead-export scans, runtime import cycles, and `git diff --check` all passed. Codex autoreview of each commit and of the full stack came back clean. CI planner tests: the global-input integration test and the dependency-hub test pass, and `ci-proof-test-inventory` passes. One source-owners planner case timed out at 120 s while three heavy planner files ran in parallel at load 50–65; it passed alone in 27.9 s.

**Inherited, not caused here:**
- The qa-lab native-hook pressure flake described above.
- `plugin-boundary-report` reports 11 compatibility records due for removal. It is date-based, and the registry and checker are byte-identical to base.
- `extensions/codex/media-understanding-provider.test.ts` "abandons app-server startup when the media request aborts" hit its 120 s deadline in a broad, loaded multi-file run. It does so identically on the base tree and passes in isolation (22 s / 10.7 s). The preload takes worker preparation out of that case, but its lazy `bounded-turn` import remains. The cause was not isolated further.
- `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-settlement.test.ts` is Linux-only. It was screened and timed on macOS, where its cases skip, so there is no Linux timing. Its preload is a top-of-file import, so the collection placement does not depend on platform.

**CI failure on head `16514e4d30a`, recorded before rerun.** Run 36971357819, job `checks-node-changed-1`. The failing case is `extensions/qa-lab/src/codex-native-hook-pressure.e2e.test.ts`, "records matched policy work through the real Gateway". It got `Process exited with code 1` with `bwrap: Can't get type of source .../workspace/.aws: No such file or directory`. The unmatched and no-policy cases passed.

This PR touches no qa-lab, sandbox, or dependency code. CI tested it merged with a `main` that already had #161446, which moved `@openai/codex` from 0.158.0 to 0.159.1. Codex 0.159.1 adds `.aws` to its protected workspace metadata names (`codex-rs/protocol/src/permissions.rs:43`), and OpenClaw sends no `.aws` deny path itself. In `codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/bwrap.rs:1213-1250`, `append_read_only_subpath_args` first checks for a transient empty metadata path, then separately calls `subpath.exists()`. A concurrent sandbox setup can create its temporary empty `.aws` mount target between those two checks, which turns it into a plain `--ro-bind` source. That target can then disappear before `bwrap` stats it. The matched-policy case is the only one that fires batches of up to 20 concurrent shell calls.

On one Linux Testbox (Actions run 36977742980), all 3 cases passed against current main `079b9cca16e4` and against this PR merged with it (`6edd5b756e36`); neither run showed the `.aws` error. So this is an intermittent upstream Codex sandbox race, not a deterministic regression from either side. The exact interleaving is unproven. The fix belongs in Codex's protected-metadata mount lifetime handling, not in this PR.

**Test cost.** No tests were added, so the CI test count is unchanged. Single-file runs of the split parts, at load 31–91: `run-main.exit` 5.4 s, `gateway-startup` 324 s, `command-dispatch` 75.6 s, `bare-root` 82.0 s, `fetch` 90.1 s, `fetch.store` 114.7 s, catalog 7.6 s, `catalog.hosted` 114.6 s. The longer runs were 81–97% transform and worker preparation on a cold or loaded cache. CI seconds will follow from this run.
